clue.text: Crashed airship — regrets account of deaths etc.

explanation.surface: A disaster headline: an airship has come down, and the clue mourns the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed' reads as a news verb but signals rearranging AIRSHIP plus REGRETS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's book records baptisms, marriages and burials in its locality, so it is a record of deaths and more.

clue.text: Law Lord in promotional material cut last item

LUD is the judge's form of address, as in 'm'lud'

explanation.surface: A senior judge is depicted in advertising copy that has been trimmed of its last item.
explanation.definitionFit: A closing piece of music played at the end of a service or work is its final item.

clue.text: Obscure singer about to enter here, dancing

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A little-known singer is about to arrive here and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like a verb or a description of the singer, but it is the definition; the singer and C sit in the middle of the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché describes something rare, exotic or far-fetched, hence obscure.

clue.text: Business chatter quietly positioned ahead of work

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet, so quietly

explanation.surface: Office gossip murmured softly before the working day begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To 'talk shop' is to chat about one's work, so the word means business talk.

clue.text: See 1

explanation.surface: Elderly men are upset as their last days approach.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the closing stage of a chess game or any contest.

explanation.definitionFit: To show something by example or picture is to depict or demonstrate it.

clue.text: Introduction to Texas, America, touring large oil industry centre

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A travel note on visiting an oil town in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa in Oklahoma was long called the oil capital of the world.

clue.text: Fraudulent behaviour in book being ignored by group

indicators.note: the letter for book is dropped from the group word

parts.note: a bracket is a group or class, as in a tax bracket

explanation.surface: A scam involving a book that a group chose to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a dishonest scheme for making money, a swindle.

clue.text: Child, swaying about, naked?

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: lurching is lurching or swaying about unsteadily

explanation.walkthrough: 'swaying about' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the synonym LURCHING; 'naked' strips L and G.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a scruffy, mischievous youngster, especially a street child.

clue.text: Relieved, went off to secure opening of unique cricket club

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.definitionFit: To succour is to give help in distress, so succoured means aided or relieved.

clue.text: Lines, including one account of a purple nature

indicators.note: the pair of line letters takes in the numeral for one

parts.note: L is short for line, so two lines are LL
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Lines of verse that give an account in purple prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale bluish-purple, so it describes something purplish.

clue.text: Story backed by university place

indicators.note: backed by means followed by, so the university letter comes after

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib

explanation.surface: A tale supported by a university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place or stead, as in 'in lieu of'.

clue.text: Careful fellow caught fish, bringing in a lot

indicators.note: the caught-and-fish letters take the word for a lot inside them

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
skate is a flat fish
a heap is a lot, a large amount

explanation.surface: An angler lands a fish and hauls in a big catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingy, penny-pinching person is ironically 'careful' with money.

clue.text: Fail to progress being late for hairdressing appointment?

definitions.meaning: golfers who fail to make the score for the weekend rounds are eliminated
arriving late at the barber's, you would lose your trim

clue.text: Recording dropped from presentation and speech

indicators.note: the recording letters are taken out of the presentation word

parts.note: a depiction is a presentation or portrayal
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.definitionFit: Diction is the manner of enunciation in speaking.

clue.text: Obstruction to hearing to increase after sources of evidence affect retrial

the sources of words are their first letters

parts.note: to wax is to grow or increase, like the moon

explanation.surface: A courtroom note: new evidence may sway a retrial and be hard to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A buildup of cerumen in the ear canal can block sound and dull one's hearing.

clue.text: Excitement? I'm in a state

indicators.note: the contraction sits inside the article plus state

parts.note: a nation is a state
I'm gives the letters IM

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to being in a state of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm in a state' reads as 'I'm agitated', which is also the definition's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness, vigour or excited spirit.

clue.text: Same rocks in slip piled up under good Lakeland location

indicators.note: in a down clue, the rest sits under the letter for good
the jumbled word goes inside the reversed slip

indicators.note: rocks means shakes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Climbing in the Lake District: rocks and slips heaped up under fine conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like scenery but is the anagram signal; 'piled up' reverses the slip word because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasmere is a village and lake in the Lake District, Wordsworth's home in Cumbria, England.

clue.text: Boat, very inferior, losing stern after spin

indicators.note: spin turns the shortened word around, reading it backwards
the stern is the back, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: lesser means inferior

explanation.surface: A poor-quality boat loses its back end after spinning around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' sounds nautical, fitting the boat, but here it just means the word's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any ship or boat.

clue.text: Part of Ireland supporting poor service is a disappointment

explanation.definitionFit: A letdown is an anticlimax or something that fails to meet hopes.

clue.text: TV detective bringing in one instrument maker

indicators.note: the detective's name takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: Luther is the BBC police drama starring Idris Elba as DCI John Luther
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A television sleuth brings in a craftsman for questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: A luthier builds stringed instruments such as violins and guitars.

clue.text: Spot military leader coming in after time

indicators.note: the officer's letters come inside the lateness word

parts.note: late means after the expected time
OC is the Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: Spotting a commanding officer turning up late.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find or pinpoint it.

clue.text: Woman picking up skills and intelligence in the US

parts.note: Ms is a woman's title
arts are skills, as in the arts of war

explanation.surface: A woman acquiring talents and brains on a trip to America.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang uses the word for brains or cleverness, as in street smarts.

clue.text: Striker in game getting flak

parts.note: a match is a game
stick means criticism, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: A football forward gets abuse during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is struck to light it, so it is literally a striker.

clue.text: T for 'tawny' and 'travel'

parts.note: tan is a tawny, yellowish-brown colour
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A spelling lesson: T is for tawny and travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tango is the code word for the letter T in the NATO phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: He will avoid infatuations, making romantic approach

explanation.surface: A man steers clear of crushes while making advances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the letters removed from PASHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a pass at someone is a flirtatious or sexual advance.

clue.text: Say too much in giving us hope

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Overstatement creeps in when offering encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush is to speak with excessive enthusiasm, to effuse.

explanation.surface: Running a reserve fund by means of old-fashioned characters.

clue.text: Pushy, but is over getting upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pushy who has finished but becomes upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtrusive behaviour is forward and intrusive, thrusting itself on others.

clue.text: Displaying most of church area provides a reasonable opportunity

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter
